answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making each identity costly to grow: a new agent must lock a refundable stake and earn endorsements from established peers before it can trade. Think of trust as an orchard, not an oasis anyone can drink from for free: planting each tree takes time, stake, and care, and a fake grove of thousands needs thousands of stakes plus endorsements honest peers will not give to strangers. A proven old identity is a relic of real work, not a name anyone can mint, so an attacker pays capital and time for every fake, while one honest identity costs almost nothing.
